entries.defect: A refusal or non-convergence on the current queue-head point is treated as a batch-wide terminal state instead of deferring that point with its reason recorded and claiming the next workable one, so a single stuck point stands the whole batch still.

The owner session is launched with a cwd inherited from a point worktree instead of being canonicalized to the main checkout, so board and ownership bookkeeping split across checkouts and the session dies of the inconsistency (point 944, measured 26.08.2026).

With a dead owner and a live delegate, the delegate's ordinary branch progress is misclassified as a foreign live writer, so the in-flight protection rule refuses owner resurrection for exactly as long as the delegate keeps working; the live delegate must be distinguished and adopted, never used as grounds for refusal.

The runaway watchdog counts a refused start that never began as a started attempt without progress, trips the three-strike pause, and after pause expiry neither predicate has changed so the identical protection-plus-watchdog loop repeats forever; only real start attempts may count and a repeating refusal must escalate outward instead of into a pause.

The documented escape from the idle-board refusal, board.mjs closing N, writes a numbered closing card that the now-projection drops for any point no longer open, so for a just-ticked point the escape never produces guard-visible state and the refusal has no exit (point 937, reproduced three times); a representable closing state must be written or preserved.

land-point runs the board step before cleanup while board publication rejects any focus naming the point its own tick just closed, so the board step can never succeed: the merge completes while branch, remote branch and worktree stay standing and the session wedges; cleanup must precede the board step or the just-closed point must be an accepted closing state.

A workflow run concluded failure with a job that never started (conclusion null, zero steps, no runner) is unclassified, and the guard hard-blocks the turn end while the only in-repo retry lives inside the never-started job's steps, so only a human rerun clears it (point 953); an external rerun or infrastructure-failure deferral path is required.

One red shared test-types stage on main rejects every point's suites simultaneously, and no path isolates the known baseline failure, routes immediately to its repair, or defers only the affected points so unaffected work can proceed (point 948).

The criticality gate's documented refusal exit requires a ledger row that no command in scripts/ can write, so an honestly filed refusal stays unsatisfiable unless a human hand-appends JSON to a tracked ledger (point 942); a supported writer for exactly that row is required.

A hard guard can forbid the only mutation capable of satisfying its own or another guard's predicate, so the session can neither act nor end its turn, and the resulting circular gate carries no timer and no outward signal; every guard must expose a reachable guard-permitted repair or deferral transition, and an unresolvable block must be a reportable event rather than a silent hold.

A lock or claim left by a process that died without releasing it stays authoritative because liveness is judged from the file rather than the process, so the SessionStart hook stands every successor down and ownership cannot be reacquired despite runnable points; the stale record must become safely reclaimable.

A stop for model unavailability is genuinely insurmountable only when no policy-acceptable serving model exists at all and the chain is permanently unreachable, but nothing distinguishes that state from a briefly failing provider, so a transient error takes the same permanent stop path as an exhausted quota.

When the boundary's successor request or the resume hook at an expired restart deadline fails silently, is absent, or consumes the clock without establishing an owner or selecting another point, nothing recovers but the 900-second OS tick; the failed handoff must itself be a recorded event and the clock must stay actionable until forward motion is confirmed.

An automatic, non-insurmountable pause or parked point is stored the same way as a user-set pause and inherits its indefinite immunity without a valid future restart clock; only a human pause may be indefinite, and every machine-set pause must carry its own enforceable expiry and escalation.

The render-verify gate blocks the turn end until a covering run exists per backend, but on a host where one backend cannot run at all the condition is unreachable and only a hand-written --defer clears it; an unreachable backend must be classified and recorded as environment rather than waited on forever.

board-publish refuses while any open point lacks a queue card and board-first-guard refuses every mutation while the board is behind, so appending a new point blocks both the board and the work unless the cards happen to be written in the right order (measured on points 948-953).

The three-lane cap combined with the rule against running tightly-coupled points in parallel can exclude every remaining queue head, idling the pool while points are open; the exclusion set must be computed and the first non-excluded point named, or the idleness reported as a stop.

A finding that cannot be filed — carrier unwritable, or the guard demanding a work-order write while the board guard blocks writes — blocks the turn end with no alternative durable sink; filing must never depend on a mechanism that can itself be blocked.

The bounded responder wakes only when there is no live owner and no honored claim, so an owner that is alive by every probe but permanently wedged suppresses the one path that could report the standstill outward; liveness and progress are conflated.

A pending claim holds the launcher back for its full lifetime even when the claiming window is left unattended and no work happens there either; a claim showing no activity must be withdrawn by the mechanism, not by a remembered rule.

An in-flight declaration expires only when its evidence stops advancing, so evidence advanced by something other than the declared work — a log written by an unrelated process, a branch advanced by another session — holds the lease and suppresses the successor indefinitely; advancement is measured on the artefact, not on the work.

A landing can remove a worktree underneath a running delegate, after which every call in that delegate is refused and its uncommitted work is unrecoverable, and the owner cannot tell a strand that died from one that finished (measured 11.08.2026); a worktree with a live process must never be removed and its removal must be refused with the pid named.

The written failure-mode table lists mechanisms individually with no composition section, so a pair that only wedges in combination — the 944/945 pair being the proof — has nowhere to be recorded and no review that would find it; the inventory needs a pairwise composition check.

Stale in-flight records continue to classify every otherwise workable point as busy after their owners have died, so selection finds no candidate; expired records must be excluded from selection or reclaimed.

After a failed landing is repaired to an idle board, board-first-guard forbids land-point's remaining cleanup mutation, so the guard and the cleanup form a circular interlock; a narrowly scoped landing-recovery mutation must be permitted.

When the selected author model is unavailable but another policy-acceptable serving model exists, routing preserves the failed selection as a global refusal instead of failing over to the acceptable alternative.

When both the owner and the sole process responsible for detecting or relaunching it are absent or wedged, no restart clock is observed despite workable points; supervision must remain externally observable and restartable rather than being a single unmonitored process.
